title: The month onion prices jumped across India
summary: In November 2012, the median onion market moved +30.8% in a month, 2.3 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 2.3σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 453 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: November 2012
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 453 markets that reported in both October 2012 and November 2012.

scenes.headline: Median move +30.8%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price jumped 30.8% in one month. 90% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 2.3× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 2.3 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Gujarat
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 19 reporting markets in Gujarat had a median change of +45.5%.

scenes.headline: Kolar
scenes.caption: Kolar (Karnataka), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹1,200 → ₹1,800 per quintal (+50.0%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
